name: Beagle SQL
tagline: Hobbyist 1990s client/server SQL database in C with its own B-tree storage; abandoned by 1999.
description: Beagle SQL was a free client/server relational database written in C by Robert Klein, with Jean-Claude Magras, starting in 1996, at a time when MySQL and PostgreSQL were still young and free SQL servers were scarce. The source shows a TCP server daemon, a yacc/lex SQL parser, its own B-tree storage layer, password authentication with SHA-1 and an interactive SQL client. Its licence allowed free use and modification, but commercial redistribution required the author's written permission, so it was source-available rather than open source in today's sense. Development stopped by the end of the decade; the code survives in a 2018 GitHub mirror of historical open-source databases.
statusNote: Abandoned in the late 1990s; only a historical source mirror remains (GitHub, 2018).

license.name: Custom licence (free use; commercial redistribution needs permission)

strengths: Compact, readable C implementation of a complete small SQL server
Useful snapshot of 1990s free database engineering
weaknesses: Only a subset of SQL and no modern security
useCases: Studying how early free SQL servers were built
